title: AI papers from the 2026-10-22 arXiv announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; ordering is inferred primarily from Hugging Face Daily Papers upvotes and placement. Citation evidence is limited for these recent papers, and no citation totals were verified.

sections.title: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models
sections.abstract: StreamEval benchmarks five kinds of interactive video generation with 300 scripted cases and reports that strong visual quality does not ensure reliable request following or state consistency.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a benchmark spanning avatar dialogue/performance, world generation, and two editing tasks, with metrics for execution, state consistency, visual fidelity, and audiovisual coordination.
sections.unique_caveat: The 300 cases are scripted; the authors identify human pairwise judgments and agreement with the rubric as a next step.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Hugging Face Daily Papers for 2026-10-22 placed it #1 with 347 upvotes at the snapshot.

sections.title: DONIC: Generalist Dexterous Bimanual Tracking Control from Human Demonstrations
sections.abstract: DONIC combines a multi-view bimanual interaction dataset with a shared reinforcement-learning and behavior-cloning tracker that reports strong reference-tracking results on unseen trajectories and held-out objects.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors contribute DONIC and the 1,575-sequence, 229-object BiHOI dataset; a single checkpoint reports 86.79% success on unseen trajectories of training objects and 57.32% on held-out objects.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors limit quantitative evaluation to simulated, reference-conditioned single-rigid-object tracking; physical-robot transfer and longer-horizon/multi-object tasks remain future work.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Hugging Face Daily Papers for 2026-10-22 placed it #3 with 124 upvotes at the snapshot.

sections.title: Cache Engineering for Agents
sections.abstract: The paper lets LLM agents manage active key-value cache directly, and reports lower inference cost with improved throughput and latency compared with history trimming/summarization baselines.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose cache-side drop and position-adjustment repos operations and the AKV serving engine; their rolling-drop policy improves average benchmark score by 1.7 points and lowers average cost by 27.7% against threshold-triggered summarization.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors leave broader cache policies, training agents under this scheme, and serving support for linear-attention models to future work.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Hugging Face Daily Papers for 2026-10-22 placed it #4 with 112 upvotes at the snapshot; independent technical coverage also discussed the design.

sections.title: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation
sections.abstract: Future Chunk Prediction adds an auxiliary training objective that predicts temporally distant video chunks, improving physical-plausibility scores over teacher-forced training without changing autoregressive inference.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that, under matched settings, FCP raises Physics-IQ from 30.4 to 33.8 for Wan2.2-5B image-to-video and from 40.6 to 44.4 for video-to-video, while leaving inference unchanged.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors did not test larger-scale or from-scratch training or longer video horizons; complementary VLM-judged benchmarks may miss subtle timing/magnitude differences, and some training footage is not released.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Hugging Face Daily Papers for 2026-10-22 placed it #5 with 111 upvotes at the snapshot.

sections.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
sections.abstract: Across 120 continued-pretraining configurations, the study finds that data, world diversity, and model size affect in-domain and cross-world game performance differently, with persistent gaps on distant worlds.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors vary four model sizes, six data budgets, and five game mixtures, reporting an early interface-learning phase with broader benefits followed by more world-specific gains.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors report limited transfer to distant worlds and conclude that continued pretraining/imitation alone is insufficient for generalist embodied agents; results come from a fixed game set and 120-condition study.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Hugging Face Daily Papers for 2026-10-22 placed it #10 with 47 upvotes at the snapshot.
